problem: Earlier LLM-based VLN agents (NavGPT, DiscussNav, MapGPT) run large closed LLMs such as GPT-4 zero-shot. This makes them costly, poorly scalable and hurt by the domain gap between LLM pretraining corpora and VLN. They also pick actions directly from noisy text descriptions of the visual scene, with no guidance on how to filter that information. NaviLLM trains an LLM but maps inputs straight to actions, with no reasoning output.
motivation: LLMs bring commonsense and interpretable reasoning to navigation. Offline use performs poorly: the paper's own tests show zero-shot GPT-4/LLaMA reasoning often gives wrong imaginations or confused filtering, and GPT-4 needs ~9.8 s per step. Following world-model theory (humans form a mental model to predict what they will see next), the authors argue that an explicit, trainable, format-constrained chain of 'imagine next observation → filter candidates → act' makes the action decision easier. Such a chain can be learned cheaply with PEFT on existing VLN data.
key_idea: Fine-tune a small open LLM (LLaMA 2 7B / LLaMA-Adapter) with parameter-efficient in-domain training so that at each step it emits a formalized navigational chain-of-thought. The chain is: imagine the next landmark (constrained to landmarks named in the instruction), select the candidate view matching that imagination, then output the action. Labels are built automatically with ChatGPT landmark extraction plus CLIP matching.
insight: Explicit disentangled reasoning beats direct action prediction (DAP) in every training setting (zero-shot, pretraining-only, finetuning-only, pretrain+finetune; Fig. 4). The two intermediate steps are both needed. On the R2R val-unseen subset with pretrain+finetune, AP alone gives SR 21.11 / SPL 14.82, AP+FI 24.44/23.78, AP+VIF 23.33/22.33, and full AP+FI+VIF 30.00/28.23 (Table 2). Training on formalized labels matters far more than raw LLM scale: zero-shot GPT-4 with free-form CoT reaches SPL 12.33 on the subset versus 48.69 for trained NavCoT-LLaMA2, which is also ~0.5 s vs ~9.8 s per step. Zero-shot LLaMA2 with the NavCoT prompt (SPL 5.79) is itself below GPT-4 with the original CoT (SPL 12.33), so the prompt format alone does not explain the gain. The base LLM's own capability still matters (LLaMA-Adapter SR 21.97 vs LLaMA 2 SR 36.40 on full val-unseen). Pretraining mainly raises OSR, while imitation finetuning drives SR/SPL. Choosing actions by CLIP-matching the generated imagination alone ('LLM & CLIP*', SR 32.23) beats zero-shot LLMs, which validates the label-generation scheme. It is still far below the trained LLM (SR 53.33), because decisions also depend on history and direction.
method: Vision-to-text system: the frozen BLIP captioner describes each navigable view's RGB image. Heading/elevation are mapped to one of six textual directions (e.g. 'turn left', 'go up') and concatenated with the caption. Each candidate gets a letter option, and 'stop' is option A.

Navigational CoT prompt: one in-context example plus the query input (instruction, lettered candidate descriptions, textual action history). The LLM must output exactly 'Imagination: U_t. Filtered observation: V_t matches the imagination. Action: a_t.' This covers Future Imagination (FI), Visual Information Filter (VIF) and Action Prediction (AP).

Reasoning ground-truth collection: ChatGPT extracts the list of object/scene landmarks from each instruction. The CLIP text/image encoders score each landmark against the ground-truth next-view image, and the argmax becomes the imagination label U*_t. The VIF label and action label are both the ground-truth action option a*_t.
Task-decomposed pretraining: FI, VIF and AP are separate instruction-following tasks per step. Training uses the summed cross-entropy L_p = L_FI + L_VIF + L_AP.

Imitation-learning finetuning: expert R2R/RxR/REVERIE/R4R trajectories are rewritten with CoT*_t labels, and the LLM is trained to generate the full chain at every step (L_f = -Σ_t CoT*_t log p(CoT_t | I, H_t, D_t)).

Parameter-efficient training: LLaMA-Adapter (LLaMA 1 7B, 1.2M trainable params) or LLaMA 2 7B with bias tuning (1.6M trainable params). Training uses AdamW (lr 0.001, wd 0.02), batch 8 on 4 V100s for ~10 h; inference runs on one V100.

setting.backbone: LLaMA 2 7B (bias-tuning PEFT) as main; LLaMA-Adapter (LLaMA 1 7B) variant; frozen BLIP captioner for vision-to-text
setting.training_data: Per-benchmark training splits, with trajectories reformulated as CoT labels: R2R train (optionally plus 12000 randomly chosen samples from the Speaker-Follower R2R augmentation data), RxR English train (26464 pairs), REVERIE train. Low-resource settings use 3000 R2R train trajectories from 61 scans and 5000 R4R train trajectories from 50 scans. Imagination labels are auto-generated with ChatGPT landmark extraction plus CLIP similarity.
setting.observation: Text only for the LLM: BLIP captions plus discretized direction of each navigable view from the panoramic RGB, the instruction, and a textual history of previous actions
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph candidate viewpoints (lettered options) plus stop

numbers_note: Several own results were left out because of the per-split variant limit. (1) Low-resource R2R val-unseen (training on 3000 trajectories from 61 scans; Table 6): NavCoT NE 7.08, OSR 37.46, SR 31.33, SPL 29.08. (2) Zero-shot NavCoT (LLaMA2)* on the 90-pair subset: NE 9.02, OSR 26.67, SR 16.67, SPL 5.79. (3) LLaMA-Adapter finetuned on the subset: NE 7.16, OSR 31.11, SR 28.89, SPL 26.59. (4) Table 2 proxy-task ablations on the subset: pretrain+finetune AP+FI+VIF gives OSR 31.11, SR 30.00, SPL 28.23. The training-setting comparison against DAP (zero-shot / pretrain / finetune) appears only in Fig. 4. Backbones for the RxR, REVERIE and R4R tables are not stated explicitly. No R2R test-unseen results are reported.
results: On R2R val-unseen, NavCoT with a PEFT-tuned LLaMA 2 7B reaches SR 36.40 / SPL 33.17, beating GPT-4-based NavGPT (SR 34 / SPL 29). With 12k extra augmentation samples it reaches SR 40.23 / SPL 36.64. It remains far below cross-modal SOTA such as ScaleVLN (81/70) and HAMT (66/61). Across RxR-En (SR 24.52 vs DAP 20.46; CLS 45.06 vs 37.19), REVERIE (SR 9.20 vs 3.12) and low-resource R4R (CLS 45.99 vs 19.73), NavCoT consistently beats its direct-action-prediction variant but trails a re-implemented IL-trained HAMT.
limitations: Converting vision to text with BLIP captions of individual candidate views loses detail and global panoramic context, which causes wrong decisions (stated by the authors). Performance stays far below cross-modal pretrained VLN models.
Imagination labels are noisy (CLIP landmark matching is ~73% accurate by human evaluation). The method also relies on ChatGPT for landmark extraction and uses English-only RxR.
Many ablations use only a 90-episode R2R val-unseen subset, where numbers are much higher than on the full split. No test-server results are given, and some tables do not name the backbone.
